answer: A stake-and-work registry resists sybils: each agent must lock a deposit and finish verifiable useful work before earning reputation. One fake identity is cheap, but spawning thousands means locking thousands of deposits and paying compute for each, so attacker cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Like an ivory tower admitting only one sonnet per author, the registry caps identities per stake, and an opal-like uniqueness check - distinct hardware or payment rails - rejects clones sharing a credential. Large fake swarms thus become unprofitable.
